items.quote: I had to act in a school play when I was about ten years old. I really didn't want to do it. But everyone had to do it so I didn't have a choice. A talent agent came and watched it and later gave me some work. It's funny because I'd always known that I wanted a movie career. I just didn't think that I would be in the movies.
items.author: Kristen Stewart

items.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models on Heterogeneous Cognitive and Biomedical Knowledge Graphs: The Role of Graph Grounding in Multi-Hop Reasoning and Hallucination Mitigation
items.abstract: This paper benchmarks LLMs on biomedical and cognitive KGs, evaluating multi-hop reasoning and hallucination. The core method involves a tiered query dataset under KG-aware and KG-agnostic conditions. The key contribution is demonstrating that general-purpose LLMs can outperform domain-specific ones, and crucially, that grounding LLMs to KGs significantly reduces hallucinations and improves reasoning accuracy.

items.title: FewStepRL: Fine-tuning Few-step Diffusion Models with Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: This paper introduces FewStepRL, a method to efficiently fine-tune few-step diffusion models using reinforcement learning. It addresses the high computational cost of traditional RL by adapting objectives for faster sampling. The core contribution lies in a systematic three-phase approach (transformation, decomposition, adaptation) that makes diverse RL objectives compatible with few-step models, enabling efficient learning.

items.title: Agent-R$^2$: Scaling Agents for Realistic Productivity Work via Real-Source Data Synthesis
items.abstract: Agent-R$^2$ tackles the challenge of training AI agents for realistic productivity tasks by introducing a novel data synthesis framework. Its core method leverages real-world occupational data, corpus evidence, and authentic web files to generate training data that reflects complex workflows and heterogeneous contexts. This approach aims to overcome current limitations and enable agents to successfully complete long-horizon, professional tasks with fine-grained requirements.
items.figure_caption: GDPval Pass@1 comparison. Agent-R 2 -4B improves the Qwen3-4B-Thinking base model by 18.6 points and surpasses several larger open-source baselines.

items.title: From Twisted Facts to Rogue Agents: Can LLMs Reliably Detect Multi-Dimensional Hallucinations?
items.abstract: This paper introduces HaluCheck, a large-scale benchmark for evaluating LLMs' ability to detect multi-dimensional hallucinations in both text and agent behaviors. The core method involves creating over 42,000 annotated instances with fine-grained labels for detection, localization, and correction. The main contribution is demonstrating that current LLMs struggle with nuanced hallucination detection, especially for agent trajectories, highlighting the need for further research and development in this area.
items.figure_caption: Representative hallucination risks in real-world LLM applications.

items.title: A Generative Model of Contextual Integrity: Appropriate vs. Inappropriate Information Sharing
items.abstract: This paper introduces a generative model simulating conversations between two LLM agents to study contextual integrity in information sharing. The core method involves observing how private information is shared or withheld based on situational norms, agent decision logic, and disposition. The key contribution is a computational framework to analyze the dynamics of disclosure and refusal in conversations, revealing how appropriate and inappropriate sharing emerges under varying conditions.

items.title: Signals, Evidence, and Context: User Scrutiny in Real-World LLM Conversations
items.abstract: This paper investigates how users scrutinize Large Language Model (LLM) responses in real-world conversations. The core method involves analyzing a large dataset of LLM-user interactions to identify patterns in user acceptance, checking, and challenging based on LLM response features like attribution and uncertainty. The main contribution highlights a significant gap between LLMs claiming to be grounded and the availability of inspectable evidence, while also revealing that user scrutiny is often concentrated and context-dependent.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1. RQ1: Response features across samples and platforms. (A) Detected feature prevalence among qualifying response pairs ( N = 368,644 N=368{,}644 ). The observed attribution-to-URL ratio is approximately 24:1; an illustrative sensitivity calculation accounting for attribution-detector precision yields approximately 10:1–20:1. (B) Platform-specific prevalence among all joined response pairs, with percentages shown in each cell. The denominators differ between panels. The measures describe features preserved in the released records and do not assess whether individual claims are adequately supported.

items.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
items.abstract: SwarmEvolve accelerates LLM-guided evolutionary search by using hundreds of low-cost agents that operate in a latent space, avoiding costly text generation. These agents form swarms, reason collectively, and share information via KV caches. The framework's novelty filter and latent-space crossover enable efficient discovery of diverse and high-scoring solutions, outperforming previous methods on various problems.

items.title: Cultural Adaptation within Repeated Social Interactions
items.abstract: This paper investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) can learn and adapt culturally through repeated social interactions, moving beyond static knowledge. The core method involves a sandbox environment where LLMs engage in ongoing interactions, demonstrating that memory mechanisms enable longitudinal learning, transfer to new settings, and multilingual norm assimilation. This work contributes by establishing a framework for continuous, interaction-driven cultural adaptation in LLMs.

items.title: Multimodal-SEA: Benchmarking AI Agent Security under Multimodal Social Engineering Attacks
items.abstract: This paper introduces Multimodal-SEA, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate the security of AI agents against sophisticated social engineering attacks that leverage forged multimodal content. The benchmark features 608 expert-designed tasks based on real-world fraud cases, covering diverse domains and attack scenarios in both Chinese and English environments. Its core contribution is providing a controlled and interactive platform for red teaming AI agents, enabling a more comprehensive assessment of their intrinsic security against adaptive multimodal social engineering.
items.figure_caption: An illustrative multimodal social engineering attack (left) and the attack harness (right), which supports attack progression and the use of prepared or dynamically constructed content.

items.title: ProQuant: Progressive Quantization-aware Training for Edge MLLMs
items.abstract: ProQuant tackles the challenge of deploying large multi-modal language models (MLLMs) on edge devices by introducing a progressive quantization-aware training framework. Its core method involves a self-relabeling scheme to bridge the distribution gap between limited fine-tuning data and pre-trained data, enabling effective low-bit quantization. This approach significantly reduces performance degradation for MLLMs at low bit-widths, making them more practical for resource-constrained environments.

items.title: RouteAlign: Aligning Task Requirements with Model Profiles for LLM Service Selection
items.abstract: RouteAlign addresses LLM service selection by aligning task requirements with model capabilities. It structures performance measurement and selection based on task demands (capability and difficulty), using historical data to build model profiles and incoming requirements to inform current decisions. This approach leads to improved task quality and cost-efficiency compared to existing methods.
items.figure_caption: Conceptual comparison of query-model matching and requirement-profile alignment for LLM service selection. The task combines coding, reasoning, and data analysis with weights of 0.50, 0.33, and 0.17 at difficulty L3. The model profiles of services A, B, and C express performance in the same capability coordinates.

items.title: Terminal-style Mathematical Modeling Bench: The First Agentic and Verifiable Benchmark for Mathematical Modeling
items.abstract: This paper introduces TB-MathModel, the first agentic and verifiable benchmark for complete mathematical modeling problems. It addresses limitations of existing benchmarks by providing real-world problems in a containerized terminal, requiring agents to produce a single JSON artifact. The benchmark's core contribution lies in its novel, one-sided scoring and two-layer feasibility verification, ensuring both accuracy against reference solutions and physical plausibility.

items.title: A Generative Foundation Model for Multimodal Tokamak Tasks
items.abstract: This paper introduces GenToka, a generative foundation model for tokamak experiments. Its core method is to jointly model diverse, multimodal diagnostic data to adapt to various plasma control and prediction tasks, rather than training separate models for each. The contribution lies in creating a reusable, adaptable model that leverages global, cross-signal information for improved performance across a range of tokamak tasks.
items.figure_caption: Overview of GenToka. (a) Unified signal representation: multimodal measurements are time-chunked and encoded with signal-specific DCT3D; context and target adapters with schema metadata yield clean context tokens and noisy target tokens. (b) Joint conditional diffusion: the same conditional Transformer denoises all requested targets jointly at each noise level while context tokens remain clean. (c) Native-space reconstruction: denoised target codes are inverse-normalized and decoded to schema-selected time series, profiles, fields, or scalar Soft-TTD scores. (d) Pretraining and task adaptation: foundation training uses co-temporal reconstruction with random context masking; each downstream schema is adapted in two stages by aligning interfaces with the backbone frozen, then refining the backbone and target pathway with the context tokenizer frozen. (e) Benchmark scope: twenty MAST tasks in six families: equilibrium reconstruction, magnetic dynamics, profile and diagnostic dynamics, long-horizon MHD-relevant dynamics, actuator action inversion, and disruption prediction.

items.title: Benchmarks as Software: Terminal-Bench and the Case for Continuous Benchmarks
items.abstract: This paper argues that benchmarks for coding agents, like LLMs, become outdated and inaccurate over time due to model improvements and infrastructure changes. To address this "benchmark maintenance debt," they propose a continuous validation workflow incorporating community feedback, agent traces, and automated checks. They demonstrate this by applying it to Terminal-Bench 2.0, identifying and fixing issues in approximately 30% of the benchmark tasks.

items.title: Enhancing Local and Global Structure in Compressed AI Agent Memory
items.abstract: This paper proposes a method to improve the compression of AI agent memories, which are stored as embedding vectors. The core method, Locality-Aware Quantization (LAQ), enhances both local neighborhood preservation and global structural integrity during compression. The contribution is a novel quantization technique that demonstrably improves memory fidelity at low storage costs, ensuring that both nearby and distant relationships between memories are better maintained after compression.

items.title: FedReason: Large Language Models as Weight-Space Meta-Aggregators for Heterogeneous Federated Learning
items.abstract: FedReason proposes using a large language model (LLM) as a meta-aggregator in federated learning to dynamically select aggregation rules for heterogeneous clients. The LLM analyzes client model weights within a secure sandbox, generates Python aggregation programs, and the server executes them, improving performance over fixed rules like FedAvg, especially under label skew.

items.title: PCBRouteAgent: How Close Are LLM Agents to Becoming PCB Routing Engineers?
items.abstract: PCBRouteAgent tackles PCB routing by mimicking human engineers, separating global planning from detailed execution. It uses a multimodal planner to generate routing strategies from board images and design data, which a detailed executor then implements using native tools. This approach achieves high success rates by allowing iterative refinement of plans based on feedback from failed routing attempts.
items.figure_caption: PCB routing connects required pads with copper traces and vias while satisfying design rules.

items.title: RM-VLM: From Natural-Language Task Descriptions to Vision-Grounded Reward Machines
items.abstract: This paper introduces RM-VLM, a method that automates the creation of reward machines (RMs) for reinforcement learning. It uses a large language model to generate an RM from a natural language task description and a vision-language model to interpret visual observations, thereby grounding the RM's propositions and enabling RM-guided policy learning without manual engineering. This contribution significantly broadens the applicability of RMs to complex, non-Markovian tasks with visual inputs.

items.title: SMART: State-based Multi Agent Reasoning Traces for Verification-oriented Problem-Solving
items.abstract: SMART is a multi-agent framework that extracts implicit state knowledge from entities within a problem context. It uses diverse LLMs and a structured prompt strategy to curate this knowledge into solution-salient premises, significantly improving validation performance on complex claims by grounding reasoning in real-world, verified information.
items.figure_caption: A complex problem’s implicit state-based reasoning using a scientific claim from SciFact Wadden et al. (2020) . We identify experts knowledgeable about participating entities and explore their state and obtain contrastive premises. We curate true premises of supporting or opposing stance and reason with these to infer the solution.

items.title: The Power of Meta Access in the Software of the Future --- Demonstrated on LLM Chat UIs and Chat AI
items.abstract: This paper introduces "meta access," a method that grants LLM chat interfaces a structured view of their own interface elements and functionalities. This allows LLMs to understand and interact with the user interface beyond just the current conversation, enabling them to find, navigate, and operate the application. The core contribution is demonstrating how meta access can transform chat UIs into unified entry points for complex tasks, while also highlighting the associated security and trust challenges.
items.figure_caption: The tutorial library, opened from the Browse tutorials entry point in the Meta Chat banner. Tutorials are grouped by task and can be started directly; each runs a guided tour of the real controls.

papers.abstract: SwarmEvolve accelerates LLM-guided evolutionary search by using hundreds of low-cost agents that operate in a latent space, avoiding costly text generation. These agents form swarms, reason collectively, and share information via KV caches. The framework's novelty filter and latent-space crossover enable efficient discovery of diverse and high-scoring solutions, outperforming previous methods on various problems.

papers.title: Cultural Adaptation within Repeated Social Interactions
papers.abstract: This paper investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) can learn and adapt culturally through repeated social interactions, moving beyond static knowledge. The core method involves a sandbox environment where LLMs engage in ongoing interactions, demonstrating that memory mechanisms enable longitudinal learning, transfer to new settings, and multilingual norm assimilation. This work contributes by establishing a framework for continuous, interaction-driven cultural adaptation in LLMs.

papers.title: Multimodal-SEA: Benchmarking AI Agent Security under Multimodal Social Engineering Attacks
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Multimodal-SEA, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate the security of AI agents against sophisticated social engineering attacks that leverage forged multimodal content. The benchmark features 608 expert-designed tasks based on real-world fraud cases, covering diverse domains and attack scenarios in both Chinese and English environments. Its core contribution is providing a controlled and interactive platform for red teaming AI agents, enabling a more comprehensive assessment of their intrinsic security against adaptive multimodal social engineering.
papers.figure_caption: An illustrative multimodal social engineering attack (left) and the attack harness (right), which supports attack progression and the use of prepared or dynamically constructed content.

papers.title: ProQuant: Progressive Quantization-aware Training for Edge MLLMs
papers.abstract: ProQuant tackles the challenge of deploying large multi-modal language models (MLLMs) on edge devices by introducing a progressive quantization-aware training framework. Its core method involves a self-relabeling scheme to bridge the distribution gap between limited fine-tuning data and pre-trained data, enabling effective low-bit quantization. This approach significantly reduces performance degradation for MLLMs at low bit-widths, making them more practical for resource-constrained environments.

papers.title: RouteAlign: Aligning Task Requirements with Model Profiles for LLM Service Selection
papers.abstract: RouteAlign addresses LLM service selection by aligning task requirements with model capabilities. It structures performance measurement and selection based on task demands (capability and difficulty), using historical data to build model profiles and incoming requirements to inform current decisions. This approach leads to improved task quality and cost-efficiency compared to existing methods.
papers.figure_caption: Conceptual comparison of query-model matching and requirement-profile alignment for LLM service selection. The task combines coding, reasoning, and data analysis with weights of 0.50, 0.33, and 0.17 at difficulty L3. The model profiles of services A, B, and C express performance in the same capability coordinates.

papers.title: Terminal-style Mathematical Modeling Bench: The First Agentic and Verifiable Benchmark for Mathematical Modeling
papers.abstract: This paper introduces TB-MathModel, the first agentic and verifiable benchmark for complete mathematical modeling problems. It addresses limitations of existing benchmarks by providing real-world problems in a containerized terminal, requiring agents to produce a single JSON artifact. The benchmark's core contribution lies in its novel, one-sided scoring and two-layer feasibility verification, ensuring both accuracy against reference solutions and physical plausibility.

papers.title: A Generative Foundation Model for Multimodal Tokamak Tasks
papers.abstract: This paper introduces GenToka, a generative foundation model for tokamak experiments. Its core method is to jointly model diverse, multimodal diagnostic data to adapt to various plasma control and prediction tasks, rather than training separate models for each. The contribution lies in creating a reusable, adaptable model that leverages global, cross-signal information for improved performance across a range of tokamak tasks.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of GenToka. (a) Unified signal representation: multimodal measurements are time-chunked and encoded with signal-specific DCT3D; context and target adapters with schema metadata yield clean context tokens and noisy target tokens. (b) Joint conditional diffusion: the same conditional Transformer denoises all requested targets jointly at each noise level while context tokens remain clean. (c) Native-space reconstruction: denoised target codes are inverse-normalized and decoded to schema-selected time series, profiles, fields, or scalar Soft-TTD scores. (d) Pretraining and task adaptation: foundation training uses co-temporal reconstruction with random context masking; each downstream schema is adapted in two stages by aligning interfaces with the backbone frozen, then refining the backbone and target pathway with the context tokenizer frozen. (e) Benchmark scope: twenty MAST tasks in six families: equilibrium reconstruction, magnetic dynamics, profile and diagnostic dynamics, long-horizon MHD-relevant dynamics, actuator action inversion, and disruption prediction.

papers.title: Benchmarks as Software: Terminal-Bench and the Case for Continuous Benchmarks
papers.abstract: This paper argues that benchmarks for coding agents, like LLMs, become outdated and inaccurate over time due to model improvements and infrastructure changes. To address this "benchmark maintenance debt," they propose a continuous validation workflow incorporating community feedback, agent traces, and automated checks. They demonstrate this by applying it to Terminal-Bench 2.0, identifying and fixing issues in approximately 30% of the benchmark tasks.

papers.title: Enhancing Local and Global Structure in Compressed AI Agent Memory
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a method to improve the compression of AI agent memories, which are stored as embedding vectors. The core method, Locality-Aware Quantization (LAQ), enhances both local neighborhood preservation and global structural integrity during compression. The contribution is a novel quantization technique that demonstrably improves memory fidelity at low storage costs, ensuring that both nearby and distant relationships between memories are better maintained after compression.

papers.title: FedReason: Large Language Models as Weight-Space Meta-Aggregators for Heterogeneous Federated Learning
papers.abstract: FedReason proposes using a large language model (LLM) as a meta-aggregator in federated learning to dynamically select aggregation rules for heterogeneous clients. The LLM analyzes client model weights within a secure sandbox, generates Python aggregation programs, and the server executes them, improving performance over fixed rules like FedAvg, especially under label skew.

papers.title: PCBRouteAgent: How Close Are LLM Agents to Becoming PCB Routing Engineers?
papers.abstract: PCBRouteAgent tackles PCB routing by mimicking human engineers, separating global planning from detailed execution. It uses a multimodal planner to generate routing strategies from board images and design data, which a detailed executor then implements using native tools. This approach achieves high success rates by allowing iterative refinement of plans based on feedback from failed routing attempts.
papers.figure_caption: PCB routing connects required pads with copper traces and vias while satisfying design rules.

papers.title: RM-VLM: From Natural-Language Task Descriptions to Vision-Grounded Reward Machines
papers.abstract: This paper introduces RM-VLM, a method that automates the creation of reward machines (RMs) for reinforcement learning. It uses a large language model to generate an RM from a natural language task description and a vision-language model to interpret visual observations, thereby grounding the RM's propositions and enabling RM-guided policy learning without manual engineering. This contribution significantly broadens the applicability of RMs to complex, non-Markovian tasks with visual inputs.

papers.title: SMART: State-based Multi Agent Reasoning Traces for Verification-oriented Problem-Solving
papers.abstract: SMART is a multi-agent framework that extracts implicit state knowledge from entities within a problem context. It uses diverse LLMs and a structured prompt strategy to curate this knowledge into solution-salient premises, significantly improving validation performance on complex claims by grounding reasoning in real-world, verified information.
papers.figure_caption: A complex problem’s implicit state-based reasoning using a scientific claim from SciFact Wadden et al. (2020) . We identify experts knowledgeable about participating entities and explore their state and obtain contrastive premises. We curate true premises of supporting or opposing stance and reason with these to infer the solution.

papers.title: The Power of Meta Access in the Software of the Future --- Demonstrated on LLM Chat UIs and Chat AI
papers.abstract: This paper introduces "meta access," a method that grants LLM chat interfaces a structured view of their own interface elements and functionalities. This allows LLMs to understand and interact with the user interface beyond just the current conversation, enabling them to find, navigate, and operate the application. The core contribution is demonstrating how meta access can transform chat UIs into unified entry points for complex tasks, while also highlighting the associated security and trust challenges.
papers.figure_caption: The tutorial library, opened from the Browse tutorials entry point in the Meta Chat banner. Tutorials are grouped by task and can be started directly; each runs a guided tour of the real controls.
